bottom_line: Do not approve unrestricted Central Asia SME-exporter onboarding. Approve conditional expansion with segment-level enhanced due diligence where SME opacity, sanctions-adjacent goods, Caspian routing, UAE-linked counterparties, and sensitive payment rails overlap.
what_changed: The markdown case packet has been projected into a machine-readable Agenda Intelligence MD-style brief so the decision, evidence mode, assumptions, scenarios, watchlist, and confidence boundaries can be audited separately from prose.
why_it_matters: The source-backed memo is easier to review when the core decision logic is available as structured data. This does not make the case externally validated, but it makes the workflow more inspectable and closer to validation infrastructure.
affected_actors: SME exporters in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
Sanctions, AML, and onboarding review teams
main_uncertainty: Whether real customer files, transaction history, UBO records, goods-classification evidence, payment-rail data, route rationale, and correspondent-bank feedback confirm or reduce the structural risk pattern.

scenarios.name: Controlled expansion
scenarios.description: Customer data, goods descriptions, route rationale, UBO evidence, and payment-rail exposure are complete enough to support lower-risk segment onboarding.
indicators: Goods descriptions and HS codes reviewed

scenarios.name: Segment restriction
scenarios.description: High-risk goods, incomplete UBO records, unexplained route changes, or opaque UAE-linked counterparties appear repeatedly in proposed onboarding segments.
indicators: Customer concentration in a narrow counterparty set

scenarios.name: Correspondent-bank pressure
scenarios.description: Banking or payment partners ask for additional explanations, reject flows, or tighten their risk appetite below the fintech's planned operating model.
indicators: New bank partner conditions on route or goods exposure

scenarios.name: Enforcement shock
scenarios.description: A new sanctions, export-control, or AML action names a relevant bank, intermediary type, commodity, route, payment mechanism, or regional financial node.
indicators: New OFAC, EU, UK, UN, or national designations
New Treasury warning on foreign financial institutions or SPFS
New export-control action affecting customer goods categories

watch_next: New OFAC, EU, UK, UN, or national designations involving regional banks, logistics companies, trading houses, payment providers, or intermediaries
OFAC or Treasury updates on foreign-financial-institution exposure, SPFS, or Russia military-industrial-base support
BIS or EU export-control updates affecting goods categories used by SME exporters
FATF, EAG, or national AML updates changing risk posture for relevant jurisdictions
Correspondent-bank requests for route, counterparty, goods, or payment-rail explanations
Customer concentration in a narrow set of UAE-linked counterparties
Increase in route changes without commercial explanation
